_comment: Written by the QA pass over data/50-power.json (c64.psu, mb.rf-modulator, c64.mains). Everything here is a change I am not allowed to apply myself: the target node lives in a fragment I do not own, or under c64.bottoms-out. `retype` and `duplicates` are extensions of the schema in README.md for the two cases a from/to merge cannot express; `note` explains anything a reviewer needs to know.

retype.why: CHECKLIST 2: 'Stranded copper conductors' is a substance with a composition, not an operation. 50-power's copy of the same thing is already kind 'material'. The description mixes the two - it names the stranding operation - so the operation belongs in a child process node if anyone wants it.
Already correct in the tree; listed only so the maintainer can see the merge above is consistent. No change needed - ignore if the file already says part.

note:
Three judgement calls in 50-power.json that the maintainer may want to overrule.

1. The bulk-capacitor construction chain was kept local. c64.psu.bulk-cap still owns its own anode-foil, electrolyte, separator and winding nodes instead of adopting mb.passives.caps.alu-electrolytic. The two are not the same account: mine is the 1980-82 ammonium-pentaborate and kraft-paper construction of the brick's 4700 uF 16 V part, the other is the general mainboard account with glycol-ether electrolytes, a wound mandrel and an ageing step. They will read as two facts about aluminium electrolytics, which is what CHECKLIST 4 warns about, but they genuinely disagree and picking a winner would lose the brick's numbers. If the maintainer prefers one construction, mb.passives.caps.alu-electrolytic is the richer node and the brick-specific facts should move onto c64.psu.bulk-cap first - that is what I did with everything else.

2. The hybrid module subtree was kept, reframed rather than deleted. mb.rf-modulator.hybrid-module is now kind 'note', named 'Illustrative hybrid module construction, not the Commodore build', confidence low, and its description opens by stating that both Commodore drawings (251025 and 251696) show a discrete through-hole board. A note with children routes through the components-only view, so the comparison survives without pretending to be a C64 part.

3. c64.psu.power-led was kept at confidence low. It is the one node in the fragment that may not be in the machine at all: the note says the 3-83 and 13-83 case markings list only 'power supply' with no indicator and that the teardown descriptions do not mention one. The brief's instruction to keep low-confidence nodes was read as covering this, but it is a part, not a statement about the industry, so the maintainer may prefer to cut it.
